text:
sasha: heads-up — saw a P95 jump in canary right after the late-bind kernel change merged (PR #4567). Canary 23 vs 22. P95 up ~2.3x across long-seq traffic. Anyone else seeing this?

jamie: yep reproduced on our internal perf job. quick profiler:
```
P95: before 78ms -> after 182ms
perf sampling hotspot:
  attention_generic_kernel 61.8%
  fused_attention_path 11.4%
  scheduler_overhead 9.6%
  kv_cache_serialize 4.2%
```

rui: that looks like kernel selector is falling back to generic attention for many shapes. I think the new heuristic in the binder picks the fused path only if contiguous layout matches — if layout changes we get a fallback that's much slower.

anya: did the PR change any weight layout code or fused op signature? I scanned the diff — it touched binder heuristics + one allocator tweak.

mike: can we get a microbench for the attention kernels across shapes? e.g. run `./tools/perf/run_attention_bench --seq 1024 --bs 8 --runs 500` on canary machine and compare. Also capture `cudaKernelTime` breakdown.

jamie: ran that quickly — generic kernel ~4.2ms per token, fused ~0.9ms. For batch shapes we mainly hit generic now.

rui: also seeing kv cache hit latency slight increase — logs show extra memcpy calls when cache warmup hits. Could be allocator alignment change from PR.

anya: @mike can you start a bisect? If it's the binder heuristic, reverting should immediately restore perf. Otherwise we need narrower fix.

mike: starting git bisect between abc123 (pre-PR) and def456 (post-PR). I'll run the perf microbench as the test. Will post interim results.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout canary-23 completed at 2024-11-03T15:12:30Z (rollout id canary-23).

oncall-bot: Alert: p95 regression detected in canary-23 (threshold 20%): measured 130% increase over baseline.

jamie: quick mitigation: I opened PR 4690 that temporarily reverts the binder heuristic change. If CI on that PR is green we can roll a hotfix.

mike: bisect update: culprit narrowed to commit def200..def456, which is the allocator alignment + small fuse condition refactor. Running a few more runs to be sure.

rui: can we avoid full revert? If it's alignment, we may fix allocator to preserve expected contiguity for fused kernels. But a revert for canary rollback is safer short term.

anya: agreement from product: pause canary rollouts until we confirm. jamie — do the rollback if PR 4690 is clean.

jamie: PR 4690 CI passed unit + basic perf smoke (not the long microbench). Kicking manual canary rollback now.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: reverting canary-23 -> canary-22 state.

mike: post-rollback quick check: p95 back to baseline numbers on our perf runner. Flamegraph looks like fused path restored.

rui: leaving a todo to instrument kernel-selector: add metrics for "kernel_chosen" counts by shape and a fallback rate gauge. Also add a CI microbench step that exercises long-seq shapes.

anya: created ticket PERF-1287 to add selector telemetry and tight microbench in CI. Assigning to eng-runtime.

jamie: summary: detected regression from binder heuristic change causing kernel fallbacks + allocator alignment side-effect. Paused rollout, reverted change, rollback confirmed. Next: bisect followups and a non-blocking fix for allocator.

sasha: thanks all — keep updates minimal here. If someone wants to own the follow-up patch + test, ping me. :thumbsup:
